source: Tai Suzuki (1956), On the Plant Distribution over Izu-Islands, Botanical Magazine Tokyo 69:598-601

source_scope.source_caveat: Obvious field-crop species were excluded, but the author states that some transplanted and naturalized plants remained; north/south element marking is acknowledged by the author to involve judgement.

source_mechanistic_context.volcanism: The article notes Toshima and Mikurajima as islands with no eruption record in the cited historical sources and argues that volcanic disturbance can eliminate locally patchy plant populations.
source_mechanistic_context.kuroshio: The article proposes changing Kuroshio position/width as a major explanation for the Miyake-Mikura floristic transition.

interpretation: A historical source that explicitly searched for an archipelago-wide plant-distribution boundary placed the principal north/south floristic transition much farther south than Oshima-Toshima. This weakens the specific alternative that the focal Oshima-Toshima response is merely a generic whole-flora biogeographic boundary by construction.
limitations: This 1956 source is historical and cannot substitute for a contemporary reviewed species-by-island matrix.
The indicator species were deliberately selected for conspicuous north/south distributions rather than sampled as an unbiased modern flora.
Taxonomy and establishment status require modern normalization before species-level occupancy analysis.
A noncoincident broad floristic boundary does not rule out habitat, source-pool, dispersal or other environmental differences at Oshima-Toshima.
claim_boundary: Use only as an external historical adversary showing that the source-defined broad floristic boundary is Miyake-Mikura rather than Oshima-Toshima. Do not treat it as a modern occupancy matrix or causal proof of a pollinator boundary.
